title: Rough around the edges, but my Open World Party-Based Action RPG is coming together
author: tribes33
selftext:
I'm making a procedurally generated open world RPG, imagine Elder Scrolls Daggerfall mixed with Dragon's Dogma and Diablo, where you play as a team of 3 characters: a Tank, a DPS and a Support

There's no fast travel, the games actually built around not having it, the games more of a fantasy life simulator where the mundane is actually the interesting part of the game, the game actually has a traversal mechanic where taking the roads and paths leads to faster world travel, but you can actually venture away from it and explore the procedural world seamlessly

One of the core parts of the game is that you're a party that expresses what they're going through, you're an actual team, the characters react to their surroundings, circumstances, enemy variety, time of day, what resources they have (or lack thereof)

It's a game entirely made in 3D, but rendered in a manner that makes it look very 2D, on Godot, it's SO buggy right now though, lots of rendering issues but I'm so happy that I can finally make something I've been dreaming of

replies.body: So are the sprites pre-generated using 3D models in Blender? I've seen this workflow quite a bit recently. I can see that it wouldn't work well with equipment swapping hence I guess you are going full 3D?

replies.author: tribes33
replies.body: Yeah it's a 3d model at an isometric camera at 8 different angles then every animation for every action on a spritesheet but that works for characters without equipment that changes. I'm changing to a 3d low poly model that's translated to a low resolution sprite in real time now cause I need to have equipment changes
